where: Section 3, heat balance formula Qtotal = mf cp,f (Tf - T) + P ΔHc + mv ΔHvap and the next line 'Cooling water flow is mw = Qtotal/(cp,w ΔTw)'
problem: One additive total is used for three different units, so the balance is wrong for two of them. In a vacuum crystallizer the flash evaporation is the cooling: the latent heat carried off by the vapour equals the sensible heat released by the cooling liquor plus the heat of crystallization, so mv ΔHvap ≈ Qsens + Qcryst. Adding Qevap again to the same side double counts and gives a false, too large cooling-water flow. In a steam-heated evaporative crystallizer heat is supplied, not removed, so steam duty is not divided by cp,w ΔTw of cooling water. Only the plain cooling case matches the worked example.
fix: Give the balance case by case. Cooling crystallizer, no evaporation: heat removed through the wall Q = mf cp,f (Tf - T) + P ΔHc, and mw = Q/(cp,w ΔTw). Evaporative crystallizer heated by steam: steam duty = heat to raise feed to boiling + P ΔHc + mv ΔHvap. Vacuum crystallizer, no external heat: mv ΔHvap = mf cp,f (Tf - T) + P ΔHc, solve for mv; external cooling water is small or zero.

where: Figure tree and lead paragraph, Section 1
problem: The lead names four classes (cooling, evaporative, vacuum, reaction), but the tree has only three branches, and the note under 'Reaction' says 'salting-out'. Salting-out is not reaction crystallization; Section 1 itself introduces it as a separate idea (adding a foreign substance that lowers solubility). A student reading the tree will conclude salting-out is a reaction.
fix: Make the tree match the text: either four branches (cooling, evaporative/vacuum, reaction, salting-out) or keep three and move 'salting-out' out of the reaction note into its own branch or note. Add 'vacuum' to the evaporative branch label if vacuum is being treated there.

problem: The clause 'vacuum supplies part of the cooling' is misleading. The vacuum does not cool anything; it only lowers the boiling point. All the cooling comes from the latent heat carried away by the evaporating solvent.
fix: Answer: solvent flashes and evaporates at low pressure; the latent heat of that evaporation is taken from the liquor, so the liquor cools itself and little or no external cooling water is needed.

problem: The chapter treats 'vacuum' as its own class in the lead and in Section 1, then the quiz answer files vacuum and draft-tube-baffle under 'evaporative'. The answer contradicts the classification given earlier in the same chapter, so a student cannot tell which list to use.
fix: State the grouping used: 'Cooling: stirred tank, Swenson-Walker. Vacuum/evaporative: vacuum crystallizer, draft-tube-baffle, forced-circulation.' Keep the same grouping in the lead, the tree and the quiz.

where: Section 3, 'Q = U A ΔTlm' and 'pumps magma'
problem: ΔTlm and magma are used without definition, in a chapter written for a student meeting these terms for the first time.
fix: Add: magma is the slurry of crystals in mother liquor; ΔTlm is the log-mean temperature difference between the magma and the coolant, log-mean of the two end differences.
